results.statement: Every sprint bead's design gives the code for each deliverable, so the developer makes no design decisions.
results.context: planning session; Draft wording by flint from Rand directive 2026-10-10; wording approved by Rand 2026-10-10; source words: "I want the plans to be rich with code samples so that the agent doesn't need to make decisions when developing."
results.deterministic_check: each sprint bead design contains a fenced code block for every numbered deliverable

relevant.instructions: Is the item a sprint bead: a unit of development work with numbered deliverables and a Design section describing code to write? A phase root or epic that lists sprints and decisions, with no code of its own to implement, is not a sprint bead.

criteria.yes: The item is a sprint bead with deliverables to implement.
criteria.no: The item is a phase root, epic or other non-sprint bead.
criteria.unclear: The item text does not show whether it is a sprint bead.

addressed.instructions: For each numbered deliverable in `item.text`, does the Design give the code or the exact edit: a fenced code block, an exact file/line replacement, or a signature followed by a `<redacted: N of M code lines are in the plan but were not sent to Jev>` marker? The redaction marker means the full code is in the plan and counts as code present. A one-line exact instruction (delete lines 1-4; replace X with Y in file F) counts as an exact edit.

criteria.yes: Every numbered deliverable has code, an exact edit, or a redacted code block in the Design.
criteria.no: At least one numbered deliverable has only prose with no code and no exact edit.
criteria.unclear: The deliverables and the Design cannot be matched up.

contradicted.instructions: Does `item.text` leave a design decision to the developer? Signs: 'choose', 'decide', 'TBD', 'as appropriate', 'if needed', 'either ... or ...' about how to build something, or a deliverable described only by its goal. A redaction marker is not a missing decision. Silence is not a contradiction.

criteria.yes: The item leaves at least one design decision to the developer.
criteria.no: The item leaves no design decision to the developer.
criteria.unclear: The text might leave a decision open but is ambiguous.
